Hi Sophie — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we have alignment: 

1) Summary of fit from today's demo
- Olive Labs' use case: customer support summarization + triage + redaction of sensitive fields at scale.
- Key constraints: sub-200ms p50 response target for short summaries, heavy tail of long chat histories, and strict redaction/PII controls for EU customers.

2) Initial model recommendations (for eval):
- LlamaX-13B (8-bit, Redwood-verified): strong latency/cost tradeoff for short summaries and fast turnaround.
- Redwood-std-30B (quantized): higher quality on long-thread context, recommended for triage/classification if hit-rate on long history is high.
- For EU-regulated traffic: consider dedicated Private deployment + KMS integration (we outlined options in the Security doc).

3) What we need from you to run a targeted eval:
- 200–500 representative prompts (real examples + edge cases) — include both short summaries and long chat transcripts.
- Mark any prompts that contain PII or regulated data (PII flag column is fine).
- Typical token limits for evaluation (we need common sequence lengths).

I attached our redaction_checklist.pdf to help you classify sensitive fields and remove direct identifiers before upload. Please either: reply with the sample CSV attached or drop files into the shared Drive folder below.

Suggested timeline:
- This week: Olive uploads first 100 prompts (by Thu)
- Next week: Redwood runs 3-model eval (LlamaX-13B, Redwood-std-30B, and a lightweight Mistral-Variant) and shares benchmarks + qualitative failure cases.

Links: Shared Drive folder for prompts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-olivelabs-prompt-bank
Benchmarks (internal): https://redwood-internal.com/benchmarks/llamax-13b-vs-std-30b

Thanks Sophie — got the CSV and the PII flags, appreciate the careful labeling. A few technical answers and proposed MA P (mutual action plan):

Technical notes:
- KV cache: by default our serving runtime isolates KV cache per-session for privacy; we persist cache only for the duration of the session request unless you opt into a customer-level cache for throughput. For your summarization workflow we recommend session-scoped cache to avoid cross-user leakage.
- Hallucination when redacting mid-output: yes, it's a known failure mode we include in our eval suite (we run targeted redaction stress tests). We'll surface the specific failure cases in the qualitative report.

Recommended eval config (to run this week once we have the 100 prompts):
- Models: LlamaX-13B (8-bit) | Redwood-std-30B (quantized) | Mistral-Lite (baseline)
- Metrics: ROUGE-L / chrF for summarization, classification accuracy for triage, tokens/sec and p50 latency (50/95/99), and a redaction-regression score (pass/fail per prompt).
- Quality checks: automated redaction stress tests + manual review of top 10 failure cases.

Mutual action plan (timeline):
- Tue (today): Redwood ingests the CSV and runs a quick smoke-run across LlamaX-13B.
- Thu: full 3-model run + quantitative report (benchmarks + latency/cost tradeoff).
- Fri next week: sync to review top failure cases and discuss production deployment recommendation.

Links & artifacts:
- Benchmark snapshot: https://redwood-internal.com/benchmarks/llamax-13b-vs-std-30b
- Prompt Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-olivelabs-prompt-bank
- HubSpot: https://hubspot.company/contacts/deal/OLIVE-2026-023

If Olive wants tighter SLAs for EU traffic we should fold the security team into the next call — happy to coordinate.
